No EEG has been performed or reported — and per the case summary, it remains “unreported/not performed”. Additionally, critical metabolic and pharmacokinetic data are missing: serum phenytoin level (to assess for subtherapeutic dosing or toxicity), glucose, sodium, magnesium, renal/hepatic function — all of which could independently cause or mimic NCSE. At Turn 15/16, the maximum turn limit is imminent; delaying diagnosis until all labs return is no longer tenable, but *diagnostic sufficiency requires at least one objective pillar* — either (a) confirmatory EEG, or (b) strong alternative exclusion supported by normal labs *plus* clinical evolution (e.g., rapid spontaneous recovery inconsistent with NCSE). Neither is present. This constitutes a critical evidentiary gap.

[DECISION] INCOMPLETE

[FEEDBACK] EEG is mandatory and urgently required to confirm or exclude NCSE — without it, the diagnosis remains speculative. Additionally, serum phenytoin level (total and free, if feasible), point-of-care glucose, sodium, magnesium, and creatinine must be obtained immediately. These five tests constitute the minimum objective dataset needed to either support NCSE (e.g., normal labs + ictal EEG) or identify an alternative reversible cause (e.g., hypoglycemia, severe hyponatremia, phenytoin toxicity). Proceeding to diagnosis without them violates diagnostic standards for altered mental status in epilepsy patients.
